 US News Agregar Clarín en X When is the next federal holiday in the US? Full schedule for the rest of 2026
 With Veterans Day wrapped up, only two statutory federal holidays remain on the official 2026 calendar. 
 From Thanksgiving Day bank and post office closures to Christmas Day schedules, here are the dates, federal workforce rules, and service impacts for the rest of the year.
 With Veterans Day wrapped up, only two statutory federal holidays remain on the official 2026 calendar. NEWSROOM CLARIN The next federal holiday in the United States is Thanksgiving Day , observed on Thursday, November 26, 2026 .
 Following the nationwide observance of Veterans Day on Wednesday, November 11, the official U.S. government calendar enters its final stretch of the year. Under federal law, Congress recognizes eleven permanent statutory public holidays , leaving American workers, financial institutions, and public agencies with only two official holidays before the new year arrives.
 The Remaining 2026 Federal Holidays
 Federal law establishes paid time off for non-essential executive branch employees, setting the benchmark for banking institutions, public school districts, and courts across the country:
 Thanksgiving Day: Thursday, November 26, 2026
 Christmas Day: Friday, December 25, 2026
 Both upcoming dates bring comprehensive nationwide closures to the U.S. Postal Service , commercial bank branch lobbies , federal and state courthouses, the Federal Reserve payment system, and Wall Street trading floors . Unlike Veterans Day —where most retailers, department stores, and supermarkets remain open— Thanksgiving Day also prompts widespread retail shutdowns , with major big-box chains like Target, Walmart, and Costco closing their doors to allow retail staff the holiday off.
 Full 2026 U.S. Federal Holiday Schedule
 Federal public holidays are designated under Title 5 of the United States Code (5 U.S.C. 6103) and administered by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM):
 New Year’s Day: Thursday, January 1, 2026
 Martin Luther King, Jr. Day : Monday, January 19, 2026
 Washington’s Birthday (Presidents' Day): Monday, February 16, 2026
 Memorial Day: Monday, May 25, 2026
 Juneteenth National Independence Day : Friday, June 19, 2026
 Independence Day: Friday, July 3, 2026 (Observed)
 Labor Day: Monday, September 7, 2026
 Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day: Monday, October 12, 2026
 Veterans Day: Wednesday, November 11, 2026
 Thanksgiving Day: Thursday, November 26, 2026
 Christmas Day: Friday, December 25, 2026
 How Federal "In Lieu Of" Holiday Rules Work
 Federal law dictates specific observational adjustments whenever a public holiday coincides with a weekend for employees working standard Monday-through-Friday schedules:
 Saturday Holidays: When a statutory holiday lands on a Saturday, government offices and financial entities observe it on the preceding Friday for pay, leave, and operational purposes. (This occurred earlier in 2026 when July 4 fell on a Saturday and was observed on Friday, July 3).
 Sunday Holidays: When a holiday falls on a Sunday, the statutory observation automatically rolls over to the following Monday.
 Because both Thanksgiving Day (always the fourth Thursday of November) and Christmas Day (falling on a Friday in 2026) land on standard weekdays, federal employees, post offices, and national banks will observe both holidays on their exact calendar dates.
 Unofficial Holidays vs. Federal Observances
 Consumers frequently confuse cultural or religious celebrations with official public holidays. While dates such as Christmas Eve (Thursday, Dec. 24) and New Year's Eve (Thursday, Dec. 31) bring early closures to financial markets or modified commercial hours, neither is a statutory federal holiday unless granted by special presidential executive order. Mail delivery and normal government operations proceed on those days unless an administration decrees otherwise.
 Looking ahead to the start of the 2027 calendar year, federal operations will pause immediately on Friday, January 1, 2027, for New Year’s Day, followed by Martin Luther King, Jr. Day on Monday, January 18, 2027.
